bottleneck: The image installs gcc and make but omits the C development headers, so every scored attempt reaches a fatal stdio.h error after fixing the intentional Makefile typo; eight attempts spend extra work installing build-essential and four never repair the environment.
change: Repair the environment by installing build-essential in the image instead of the incomplete gcc-only package set. This structural setup repair removes the unrelated package-install stage and leaves all BLOG layout inference and reader implementation to the student.
restore: Restore the original gcc and make package list in environment/Dockerfile to withdraw this setup repair; no task requirement, fixture, solution logic, or verifier check changes.
prediction: Attempts will proceed directly from correcting the Makefile to compiling and exercising the reader instead of reacting to a missing stdio.h and installing a toolchain. This permits more time for the still-required 64-bit timestamp inference; the prediction is refuted if fresh attempts still report missing standard C headers or if none advances beyond the same timestamp-width mistake.
